questions.stem: A client has symmetric pain and swelling in both hands with prolonged morning stiffness. Which finding is more characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis than osteoarthritis?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Joint pain that is only activity-related and consistently improves with rest, without inflammatory stiffness","B":"Symmetric involvement of small joints, prolonged morning stiffness, and possible systemic inflammatory symptoms","C":"Disease limited to weight-bearing joints with no autoimmune component or extra-articular manifestations","D":"A disorder restricted to older adults and characterized by isolated cartilage degeneration without inflammation"}}
questions.rationale: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease. It commonly affects small joints of the hands and feet in a symmetric pattern and may cause prolonged morning stiffness, fatigue, and low-grade fever. Osteoarthritis is primarily degenerative and is more commonly associated with pain related to joint use and shorter periods of morning stiffness.
questions.source_detail: Symptoms of Rheumatoid Arthritis: symmetric pattern; morning stiffness longer than 30 minutes; fatigue and occasional fever. Last reviewed by NIAMS current page accessed 2026-08-14.

questions.stem: A client with an acute gout flare in the great toe is prescribed colchicine. Which explanation of colchicine is most accurate for the current flare?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Colchicine reduces the inflammatory response to urate crystals during an acute gout flare","B":"Colchicine dissolves deposited urate crystals directly and permanently lowers the serum urate level","C":"Colchicine is the preferred urate-lowering drug for maintaining serum urate below the treatment target","D":"Colchicine treats gout by eradicating a bacterial infection within the affected joint"}}
questions.rationale: Colchicine is an anti-inflammatory treatment used for gout flares. It does not directly dissolve urate crystals or serve as a urate-lowering therapy. Importantly, colchicine can also be used as anti-inflammatory prophylaxis when urate-lowering therapy is initiated, so the prior wording that implied it has no preventive role was removed.
questions.source_name: American College of Rheumatology — 2020 Guideline for the Management of Gout
questions.source_detail: 2020 ACR Gout Guideline: colchicine is an accepted first-line anti-inflammatory option for gout flares; anti-inflammatory prophylaxis such as colchicine is recommended when initiating urate-lowering therapy for at least 3–6 months.

questions.stem: A client reports months of widespread pain, fatigue, poor sleep, and difficulty concentrating. No alternative inflammatory or structural diagnosis has been identified. Which condition is most consistent with this presentation?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Fibromyalgia, which can cause chronic widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and cognitive symptoms","B":"Rheumatoid arthritis, because absence of objective inflammatory findings establishes rheumatoid arthritis","C":"A normal aging process, because persistent widespread pain and cognitive symptoms are expected with age","D":"An acute infection, because months of stable widespread pain are typical of an untreated acute infection"}}
questions.rationale: Fibromyalgia is a chronic disorder characterized by widespread pain and commonly includes fatigue, sleep disturbance, and cognitive difficulty. There is no specific laboratory or imaging test that confirms fibromyalgia; testing may be used to evaluate for other causes. The earlier wording was tightened so that normal inflammatory markers or imaging are not presented as diagnostic criteria by themselves.
questions.source_detail: NIAMS overview and diagnosis pages: chronic widespread pain, fatigue, sleep problems and cognitive difficulties are common; there is no specific laboratory or imaging test for fibromyalgia. Last reviewed May 2024; accessed 2026-08-14.

questions.stem: A nurse is assessing a client for possible Parkinson disease. Which finding is most consistent with the core motor syndrome?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Bradykinesia accompanied by resting tremor and/or rigidity","B":"Abrupt ascending paralysis that resolves spontaneously within hours","C":"Isolated cognitive impairment without any motor abnormalities","D":"Sudden episodic weakness with complete recovery between attacks"}}
questions.rationale: Parkinson disease is characterized clinically by bradykinesia together with other parkinsonian motor features such as resting tremor or rigidity. Symptoms usually develop gradually rather than as abrupt, fully resolving neurologic episodes.
questions.source_detail: NINDS Parkinson disease overview: motor manifestations include resting tremor, rigidity and bradykinesia; Parkinson disease is progressive. Accessed 2026-08-14.
